workItem.goal: Let a terminal user save, list, compare and explicitly delete named dependency baselines with readable human output and deterministic JSON while preserving project, input, revision, scope, coverage and failure meaning.
workItem.writeBoundary: Only files owned by ramify/cli beneath subs/cli/src/, excluding subs/cli/module.ramify. Provisional test fakes for missing dependencies remain in ramify/cli owned tests.
excludedWork: save, list and delete command implementation in the first iteration
ramify/daemon shared service, persistence, compatibility, corruption, interruption and storage-limit behavior
ramify/analysis comparison computation or changes to dependency meaning
new modules, module.ramify edits, cross-owner contracts and cross-branch writes
claims of service or feature completion from a provisional fake

firstIteration.goal: Deliver the terminal-facing `baseline compare <name>` grammar, human rendering, deterministic JSON rendering and exit behavior against an injected provisional dependency, so a user can understand complete changes and honest incomplete or unavailable outcomes while the consumer records the behavior a real shared service must later provide.
acceptance: The CLI accepts `baseline compare <name>` with existing root selection and output conventions: human output by default and JSON only with `--format json`. It rejects missing, duplicate or ambiguous arguments before connecting and documents the command in help.

For a complete supplied comparison, human output names the baseline, identifies both analyzed inputs or revisions and production scope, and reports added and removed modules plus added, removed and changed directed consumer/provider relationships.

A changed relationship shows labeled before and after values for every supplied dependency count and classification. Historical and current evidence are distinguishable; a removed module or relationship remains inspectable in terminal detail.
JSON output is one versioned document with stable field and collection ordering for identical supplied input, including both-side identities, coverage and qualified change status.

A sufficiently complete no-change comparison reports no dependency changes. Partial or unavailable coverage never reports a clean result or treats unobserved relationships as proven removals; observed differences may be clearly qualified.

Missing or deleted baselines, incompatible or corrupt data, retryable current-input races, and resource-limit refusals produce distinct readable human and JSON results with non-success exits. Crashes, timeouts and malformed submissions are adapter events outside the semantic outcome protocol, and ordinary compile or test failures are resolved within the invocation.
The command uses an injected provisional dependency only. It does not scan source, compute dependency meaning, access baseline files directly or fall back to batch analysis.
Focused CLI tests, root type checking, build and the Ramify self-check pass after implementation. These are future evidence, not existing results.

Even when all compare-iteration acceptance passes, the semantic outcome is `partial-with-needs`: `iterationCompletion` records the completed compare slice, `localContinuation` retains save/list/delete, and `externalNeeds` retains replacement of the provisional fake by real provider behavior.
requiredEvidence: CLI grammar tests for valid and invalid baseline compare invocations before dispatch.
Owned command tests with a provisional injected fake for complete, no-change, partial, unavailable, missing, incompatible, corrupt, retryable and resource-limit results in human and JSON formats.
Repeated JSON byte comparison for identical logical results supplied in different collection orders.
From /ramify: `npm run build` followed by `npm run check:self`.
A diff review confirming all writes remain in ramify/cli and subs/cli/module.ramify is unchanged.
notCompletionOf: terminal save, list or delete operations
a real shared service delegation or contract
durable persistence, restart behavior or storage isolation
comparison computation and coherent current-revision selection
browser behavior, cross-surface agreement or the feature

Follow current parsing, injected-service, formatting and exit semantics.
Confirm the existing boundary without changing it.
Extend complete-invocation grammar and preserve validation before dispatch.
Use existing dispatch, exception and output boundaries.

knownExternalNeeds.behavior: Return one project-scoped named-baseline comparison against a coherent current production dependency analysis, including complete, qualified, unavailable, missing, incompatible, corrupt, retryable and resource-limit results.
evidence: The request requires terminal comparison with human and deterministic JSON output identifying both inputs and coverage.
The accepted map records terminal-baseline-interface consuming shared-baseline-service through terminal-service-vocabulary.
Current subs/cli/src/arguments.ts uses human output by default, accepts only `--format json`, validates before dispatch and has no baseline command.
evidenceToCreate: CLI tests exercising the information and states needed by both output forms
a provisional fake call log showing root, baseline name and requested operation
a final consumer-side result-shape inventory in the iteration report
constraints: Do not nominate another owner, prescribe transport methods or fix a foreign API in the need.
The eventual result identifies both sides, scope and side-specific coverage and retains bounded historical/current evidence.
A provisional fake proves consumer behavior only and must be replaced before delegation or feature completion.

localContinuation: Add save, list and explicit delete grammar and output in later iterations after compare establishes shared vocabulary needs.
Replace the provisional test dependency with the reviewed shared service surface when available.
Add real-service and restart acceptance after providers exist.
rationale: ramify/cli is an actual end-user consumer. A compare-only iteration fixes observable grammar, output and exit behavior while eliciting provider needs through executable evidence.

The browser workflow is also required. Terminal compare goes first because it can establish deterministic machine and human result meaning without simultaneously needing browser state, transport and rendering providers.
Save, list and delete remain in the work-item goal but are deliberately excluded from the first iteration.

The initial Stage-B draft selected ramify/presentation/project-view as a small pure renderer. Coordinator review rejected it because the accepted map makes it a provider consumed by ramify/explorer, violating the highest-consumer rule. The corrected decision starts at ramify/cli.
